capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

For the arithmetic-function identity, induct on the finite set \(t\). When adjoining a prime \(p\), the product of the remaining distinct primes is coprime to \(p\); multiplicativity then gives
\[
f\!\left(p\prod_{q\in s}q\right)=f(p)\,f\!\left(\prod_{q\in s}q\right),
\]
and the induction hypothesis finishes the product formula.

For the equivalence, observe that its left side is a general fact: coprimality is preserved under arbitrary natural powers. Prove the right side independently using the standard binomial irreducibility criterion for \(X^N-a\), with \(N=p^n\). The only prime divisor of \(N\) is \(p\), so the criterion reduces exactly to \(a\notin K^p\), expressed as \(\forall b,\ b^p\ne a\). The assumptions \(n\ne0\) and \(p\ne2\) ensure \(N>1\) and eliminate the exceptional \(4\mid N\) clause in the general criterion. Since both universally quantified propositions hold, assemble the required `Iff`.
